title: Stash Live — Setup flow and dashboard screens (V1)
summary:
A guided five-step setup — sign in, install & pair the extension, add an AI key, rehearse, join Meet — rendered in the existing editorial light-mode language (warm alabaster #FBF9F6 canvas, deep espresso #1A1512 type, #fb8500 accent used only for the 'you are here' marker and live/expiring states, Cormorant Garamond display, Inter UI, JetBrains Mono for eyebrows and telemetry). Everything is built from primitives already in src/app/components/ui so implementation is cheap: button, badge, switch, radio-group, tabs, progress, input, alert.

The spine is a persistent sticky checklist. I offer two shapes for it: a 296px left rail (recommended — it survives long scrolling pages like the six-step install without the progress leaving the viewport, and it reuses the DashboardShell sidebar rhythm) and a full-width top stepper (more editorial, but the progress scrolls away). The complete state is included so the flow visibly ends rather than trailing off.

The install screen is treated as the highest-risk moment. Two paths sit behind a tab pair: one-click Web Store, and an interim 'install from a file' path rendered as six numbered steps where four of them carry a faithful CSS reproduction of what the user will actually see — chrome://extensions with the Developer mode switch, the same page with the three grey buttons revealed and 'Load unpacked' ringed in accent, and the folder picker with the right directory selected. The failure screen quotes Chrome's own error text in mono, translates it into one sentence of plain English, then gives three numbered actions; three other common failures (admin policy, wrong browser, folder deleted) are covered as secondary notes so there is no dead end.

The AI-key panel covers all five states asked for. Validation is framed as three visible checks (format → reachable → provider accepted) so a failure says which stage broke; the error copy names the likely cause (partial copy) and gives two ordered fixes, with quota / network / wrong-provider variants below it. The configured state never re-displays the key — only last four, model, added-by and usage, with replace / test / remove. Notion appears only after the key succeeds, badged Optional, with 'Continue to rehearsal' as the primary button and Connect as the outline one, so skipping is the default-looking path rather than a failure.

Rehearsal is split into three beats — teaching the chord on physical keys with a hold indicator, the live listening state with transcript and mic level, and the payoff with a real card composited on the user's camera plus a before/after pair — and a fourth degraded state where a clearly labelled static fixture stands in and the CTA routes back to install. Join Meet states the two Meet-side surprises as a pre-flight list before the user clicks anything, then walks the camera re-selection with reproductions of Meet's own kebab menu and device dropdown, and handles the 'camera already busy' case as a calm three-step recovery rather than an error.

Trigger mode presents both modes as equals with a 'Good for' / 'The catch' pair each, sub-settings nested under whichever is active, and a green in-meeting confirmation that the change is already live; a third variation shows the confirm dialog for switching mid-call. The cards library distinguishes ephemeral AI cards by dashed accent edges, a 'Written by AI' badge, a countdown meter and a Keep it / Edit / Discard action row, against solid-edged saved cards with a source badge, phrase chips and an enable switch — recommended as two labelled zones rather than one mixed grid, because the expiry rule only needs explaining once per zone.

All in-video card previews here deliberately stay minimal; the card visual system itself is owned by the parallel card-system design set.
